source.citation: Tsuboi K., Maruta K., Takahashi S., Ihara T., Bhattacharjee S., 'Effect of Ambient Gas on Flammability Limit of Flat Materials in Microgravity', Trans. JSASS Aerospace Tech. Japan 14 (ists30) (2016) Ph_1-Ph_6
source.transcription: manual, from pdftotext -raw of the cached PDF; values and strings exactly as printed
source.acknowledgment: conducted as part of the SOLID COMBUSTION and FLARE projects supported by JAXA

campaign.platform: voo parabólico (Diamond Air Service), ~20 s de microgravidade; LOC em 1g com propagação descendente no mesmo aparato
campaign.geometry: folha plana fina, 0,125 mm de espessura, 8 cm × 2 cm
campaign.flow: fluxo oposto forçado, 0 a 20 cm/s (ventilador de sucção)
campaign.ambient: O2 em gás de balanço N2, CO2 ou Ar; câmara fechada
campaign.ignition: fio Ni-Cr na extremidade a jusante, 10 s antes do início da microgravidade
campaign.measured: LOC (1g, descendente), MLOC e Vcr (microgravidade), taxa de propagação (mm/s, câmera visível), comprimento de pré-aquecimento (IR)

definitions.LOC: minimum oxygen concentration in which steady downward spread is achieved (normal gravity)
definitions.MLOC: minimum limiting oxygen concentration observed in microgravity while varying the opposed flow velocity
definitions.Vcr: critical opposed flow velocity at which the MLOC is observed
definitions.deltaO2: MLOC - LOC as printed (negative = more flammable in microgravity)

notesFromText: N2: the LOC predicted 17.0 % is the calibration point of the model (LOC in 1g is an input), not an independent prediction.
The authors state the simplified model underestimated the MLOC in all balance gases (safe-side prediction).
